reason: Only operators whose version is the one meant. >=, ~=, == and ^ name the lowest version a project means (requires-python, package.json); >3.11 and <4 name versions it does not, and a range like >=3.11,<4 would be half-read. A bare ~ is excluded because a quoted '~5' in prose means 'about five'. Found adopting asof on chesterton, where '>=3.11' split against 'Python 3.11+'.
